The axes and where the bounds come from De Jong 1975 · Grefenstette 1986 · Schaffer 1989 · Miller & Goldberg 1995 · Such et al. 2017
  • Hidden 8 · 16 · 32 · 64 — tanh units — 8 / 32 / 64 vs 16; is a bigger brain faster to evolve?
  • Population 10 · 30 · 100 — De Jong 50–100, Grefenstette 30, Such et al. 1000 — 30 and 100 vs 10 (×3 / ×10 compute)
  • Elite 1 · 4 · 6 — Such et al. keep exactly 1 elite; classic 1–10 % — 1 and 6 vs 4
  • Tournament 2 · 5 · 8 — k=2 is the weakest pressure; Harik et al. k=4–8 converge faster — 2 and 8 vs 5
  • Crossover 0.0 · 0.7 · 0.95 — De Jong 0.6, Grefenstette 0.95, Such et al. none — 0 and 0.95 vs 0.7
  • Mutation rate 0.005 · 0.15 · 0.5 — binary-GA optimum ~1/L (≈0.003), real-valued NE mutates every gene — 0.005 and 0.5 vs 0.15
  • Mutation σ 0.02 · 0.15 · 0.5 — Such et al. σ 0.002–0.005 on deep nets, tiny nets 0.1–0.5 — 0.02 and 0.5 vs 0.15
  • Anneal 0.3 · 0.5 · 1.0 — post-first-win mutation shrink; Such ≈0.45×, 1.0 = off — 0.3 and off vs 0.5 (win rate only; 0.5 beat 0.8 in 6/6 sweeps)
  • Init σ 0.25 · 0.5 · 1.0 — Xavier gives σ≈0.27 for 14 inputs — 0.25 and 1.0 vs 0.5
  • Action feedback False · True — previous (move, jump) fed back as 2 inputs — timing memory for wall-jumps
  • Memory 0 · 2 · 3 — Jordan memory units: 2 or 3 extra outputs looped back as inputs next frame

One-factor-at-a-time isolates each knob's effect but ignores interactions — the recommended config is the per-axis composite; --confirm probes it once to check.
